summary: This PR adds a real Work Progress Report feature to PROJEXA: a pure computation module (work-progress-report.ts) with correct Prev/Current/Total math verified against the SUCCESS_CRITERIA scenario, a report API route that reuses exactly the same callVeridian() paths/params as existing proxied routes (verified by direct comparison against /api/scope, /api/attendance, /api/vendors, /api/labour-roster, /api/work-progress/activities), and a new work_progress_photos table + Supabase Storage bucket that closes the disclosed PR #54 photo-upload gap via best-effort sync-time upload that does not alter the existing tested sync/retry/mutex semantics. RLS policies on both the table and storage.objects follow this repo's established organization_id-via-memberships pattern, auth/org scoping in the new routes matches every other route in this codebase (requireAuth + org-scoped VERIDIAN API key, no re-derived per-project authorization, consistent with existing convention), and the FK-by-value pattern for the cross-database VERIDIAN entry reference is reasonably documented. No security vulnerabilities found (storage path segments are opaque object keys, not filesystem paths, so the user-controlled veridianEntryId/filename segments cannot traverse outside the caller's own org-prefixed RLS-enforced namespace). No .github/workflows/** changes. Correctly tier2 (touches schema.ts, drizzle/*.sql, and RLS) and the migration is honestly disclosed as not-yet-applied live, consistent with this repo's prior migrations.
issues: Cross-repo dependency: full report output (scope-wise rows need lineItems, category-wise needs categories) depends on the companion compliance-tracker PR #608 being merged and deployed first. Code degrades gracefully (empty arrays, 'Uncategorized' fallback) rather than crashing if PR #608 lands after this one, but the report will silently show no scope-wise/category-wise data until both PRs are live -- sequence the merges together and verify end-to-end once both are deployed.

Queued photo upload on sync is fire-and-forget with no retry/durability: the main entry is removed from the local IndexedDB queue as soon as it syncs, before the photo upload promise resolves, so if the tab/browser closes in that window the photo is silently lost even though the entry synced successfully. This is disclosed in code comments as an intentional best-effort tradeoff, but there's no user-facing indication when a photo upload actually fails after the entry synced (only a console.warn).

drizzle/0013_work_progress_photos.sql is not applied to any live database yet (no Supabase DB/Management API credentials in the sandbox, same disclosed constraint as drizzle/0011) -- a human with real Supabase access must apply the migration (including the storage bucket insert and storage.objects policies) before photo upload works end-to-end in production.
